section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single simultaneous multiple regression analysis (no Study 1/Study 2 labels) testing whether weight-loss talk and exercise talk predict body appreciation while controlling for BMI. Results are based on 138 participants and show BMI negatively predicts body appreciation (β = −.32), weight-loss talk predicts lower body appreciation (β = −.37), and exercise talk predicts higher body appreciation (β = .23).
section_summary.evidence_source: To test the hypothesis that weight loss talk would negatively predict body appreciation and exercise talk would positively predict, a simultaneous multiple regression analysis was specified. Owing to missing responses, the results are based on 138 participants. Consistent with previous research, increased BMI was associated with less appreciation of one's body when controlling for body-related talk, variance inflation factor (VIF) = 1.02, B = −.07, standard error (SE) = .02, β = −.32, 95 percent CI: (−.47, −.17), p < .01. Moreover, as hypothesized, increased talk about weight loss and dieting predicted less appreciation of one's body, VIF = 1.08, B = −.07, SE = .01, β = −.37, 95 percent CI: (−.53, −.21), p < .01, whereas increased talk about exercise predicted more appreciation of one's body, VIF = 1.07, B = .03, SE = .01, β = .23, 95 percent CI: (.07, .39), p < .01.
